skill.name: ssh
skill.description: SSH command patterns for remote access, file transfer, tunneling, key management, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Use SSH safely for remote access, transfers, tunnels, jump hosts, and key workflows.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown examples for standard SSH administration, not executable code or hidden malware. The remaining confirmed risks involve sensitive SSH key paths, ssh-agent usage, host trust file changes, tunneling, and agent forwarding that require explicit user authorization and safer guidance.

remediation.issue: Private SSH key paths are used in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before any command touches ~/.ssh private keys, and require explicit confirmation before running ssh-add or identity-file commands.

remediation.issue: Agent forwarding is enabled in a sample configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Change the default example to ForwardAgent no and document enabling it only for specific trusted hosts.

remediation.issue: Host keys are appended to known_hosts without fingerprint verification.
remediation.suggestion: Add steps to verify host key fingerprints through a trusted channel before writing to known_hosts.

remediation.issue: Tunneling examples can bypass network boundaries or expose local services.
remediation.suggestion: Add authorization warnings and scope guidance for local, remote, dynamic, and jump-host forwarding commands.

semantic_findings.title: Agent Forwarding Enabled in Example Configuration
semantic_findings.description: The SSH config example sets ForwardAgent yes. Agent forwarding can expose the local SSH agent to a compromised remote host and should be disabled unless explicitly needed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exact configuration directive is present and is a known SSH security risk when used broadly.

semantic_findings.title: Host Key Trust Added Without Verification
semantic_findings.description: The known_hosts example pipes ssh-keyscan output directly into the trust file. This can trust an attacker-controlled key during a man-in-the-middle attack if fingerprints are not verified out of band.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command directly appends scanned host keys to known_hosts and the surrounding text does not instruct fingerprint verification.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Port Forwarding Can Expose Local Services
semantic_findings.description: The remote forwarding example maps a local service to a remote port. This is legitimate SSH behavior but can unintentionally expose local development services to users on the remote host.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example clearly documents ssh -R remote forwarding; exposure depends on server policy and bind settings.

content.value_statement: Remote server access often requires exact SSH syntax and careful key handling. This skill provides practical SSH patterns for connections, transfers, tunnels, jump hosts, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Shows SSH connection commands for default ports, custom ports, identity files, and host aliases.
Provides SCP and rsync examples for uploading, downloading, and synchronizing files.
Explains local, remote, dynamic, and jump-host SSH tunneling patterns.
Documents SSH key generation, ssh-copy-id, ssh-agent, and macOS keychain usage.
Includes known_hosts maintenance, verbose debugging, and SSH security tips.
limitations: Does not verify that a user is authorized to access a target host.
Does not validate host fingerprints before known_hosts changes.
Does not manage cloud credentials, firewall rules, or server-side SSH policy.
Examples use placeholders and must be adapted to the user environment.

use_cases.title: Connect to production hosts
use_cases.description: Use host aliases, custom ports, and identity files to connect to approved servers with repeatable commands.

use_cases.title: Transfer release artifacts
use_cases.description: Copy files or synchronize directories with SCP and rsync while preserving a clear command history.

use_cases.title: Debug private services through tunnels
use_cases.description: Create local or jump-host tunnels to inspect databases, web services, or admin tools behind private networks.

prompt_templates.title: Connect to a server
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the SSH command to connect to user@hostname on the default port. Explain each part briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Copy a directory safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Give me an rsync command to copy ./local/ to user@host:/remote/path/. Include a dry-run command first.

prompt_templates.title: Create a jump-host tunnel
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me connect to an internal server through a bastion host using SSH ProxyJump. Use placeholders for all hostnames.

prompt_templates.title: Review my SSH configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SSH config for security risks, especially agent forwarding, key paths, multiplexing, and host key handling.

output_examples.input: I need to copy a file to a server.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends an SCP upload pattern with placeholders for the local file, remote user, host, and destination path.

output_examples.input: I need to access a remote database locally.
output_examples.output: The skill explains a local SSH tunnel and identifies which local port maps to the remote database endpoint.
The skill shows how to remove a stale known_hosts entry and reminds the user to verify the new host fingerprint.

best_practices: Confirm authorization before connecting to any host or creating any tunnel.
Verify host fingerprints before adding keys to known_hosts.
Use passphrase-protected Ed25519 keys and avoid broad agent forwarding.
anti_patterns: Do not run private-key commands without explicit user confirmation.
Do not add ssh-keyscan output to known_hosts without verification.
Do not use tunnels to bypass organizational network policy.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to servers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command patterns. Users must authorize and run commands in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it help with SSH keys?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows key generation, ssh-copy-id, and ssh-agent patterns, but private key handling needs explicit care.

faq.question: Does it support file transfer?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes SCP and rsync examples for uploads, downloads, recursive copies, and dry runs.

faq.question: Can it create SSH tunnels?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers local, remote, dynamic SOCKS, and jump-host forwarding patterns.

faq.question: Is agent forwarding safe?
faq.answer: Agent forwarding can be risky on untrusted hosts. Enable it only for specific trusted systems when required.

faq.question: Should I verify known_hosts entries?
faq.answer: Yes. Verify host key fingerprints through a trusted channel before adding or replacing known_hosts entries.
